questions.question: A workflow always validates a document, extracts one fixed schema, and verifies the fields. What is the strongest starting architecture?
options: A deterministic typed pipeline
An open-ended tool-using agent
A multi-agent supervisor
A durable graph with an approval interrupt
questions.explanation: The path and operations are known before execution. A deterministic pipeline is easier to test and operate without adding model-controlled routing.

questions.question: Which requirement most clearly justifies a custom LangGraph instead of one bounded LangChain agent call?
options: The response should use structured output
The model must choose among three read-only tools
The workflow must pause for approval and resume after a worker restart
The application needs a system prompt
questions.explanation: A durable approval boundary requires explicit persisted state and resume behavior, which is a stateful orchestration concern.

questions.question: What is the difference between a LangGraph checkpointer and a store?
options: A checkpointer persists thread execution state; a store holds application-defined data across threads
A checkpointer stores model weights; a store stores prompts
A checkpointer is only for logs; a store is only for metrics
There is no operational difference
questions.explanation: Checkpoints support thread continuity and recovery. Stores represent longer-lived application memory outside one thread's graph state.

questions.question: A payment tool times out after it may have committed a refund. What should the workflow do first?
options: Replay the entire chain with a new operation key
Reconcile the payment state using the original operation key
Ask the model whether the refund probably succeeded
Discard the checkpoint and start a new thread
questions.explanation: Timeout leaves completion ambiguous. Reconciliation with the authoritative service prevents a blind retry from creating a duplicate effect.

questions.question: Why are nested traces more useful than one root success log for an agent run?
options: They prove every model answer is correct
They identify which model, tool, checkpoint, or policy boundary produced latency or failure
They remove the need for offline evaluation
They automatically authorize tool calls
questions.explanation: A trace preserves causal stage evidence. Quality still needs evaluation, and authority still needs deterministic policy.

questions.question: Which deployment shape best supports long queued runs whose API traffic and execution load scale differently?
options: A scale-to-zero request function with in-memory state
Separate API servers and durable queue workers
One browser tab that owns the run
A cron job that replays every request
questions.explanation: Separating admission from execution lets each tier scale on the correct signal while durable state and a task queue preserve long-running work.
